extracted.intended_audience: Researchers invited to peer review manuscripts for PLOS Global Public Health
extracted.subtask_short: PLOS Global Public Health peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for reviewers assessing original research manuscripts submitted to PLOS Global Public Health, including procedural expectations, ethical requirements, and detailed points to assess about validity, methods, reporting, and writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepting a review invitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Accept an invitation only if you have the knowledge, time and objectivity necessary to provide an unbiased assessment of the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the links in the invitation email to accept or decline. If you accept, you are committing to provide an unbiased assessment; decline if you lack expertise, time, or objectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permission to publish reviewer report
rubrics_metrics.description: In agreeing to complete a review, you also give permission to publish your review under a Creative Commons Attribution CC BY license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you do not wish your review to be published, consider whether you want to sign or proceed; you may choose to sign (see signed peer review) which will reveal your name if the authors publish peer review history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review model: single-anonymized
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS Global Public Health practices single-anonymized peer review by default: reviewers will know the authors’ names, but reviewers’ names are not shared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your review will appear in the editorial decision letter where it can be read by authors and other reviewers; your identity will remain anonymous unless you choose to sign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signed peer review (optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers can choose to sign their name to their review when submitting it; if signed, authors and other reviewers will see the reviewer’s name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authors publish their peer review history, signed reviewer names will accompany comments alongside the published article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portable reviews (transfer between PLOS journals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews may accompany a manuscript if authors transfer it to another PLOS journal; reviewers may be asked to re-review by editors at another PLOS journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers for any PLOS journal should be willing to have their reviews considered by editors of another PLOS journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Published peer review history (authors' choice)
rubrics_metrics.description: If authors decide to publish their peer review history, the editorial decision letter and your review will appear alongside the published article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your name will not appear in the published peer review history unless you chose to sign your review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaring competing interests
rubrics_metrics.description: A competing interest is anything that interferes with or could be perceived as potentially interfering with a thorough and objective assessment. Do not accept a review assignment if you have a competing interest, or don’t feel able to give an objective assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common examples: recent/current collaboration with any of the authors; direct competition or history of scientific conflict with any author; an opportunity to profit financially from the work. If unsure, contact globalpubhealth@plos.org. If asked to review despite a potential competing interest, declare it when you submit your review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crediting collaborators / co-reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: If you had help completing the review (co-reviewing), you must share your collaborator’s name with the journal when you submit the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter the collaborator’s name in question 2 under 'Confidential comments to Editor' or email the journal. Do not include the collaborator’s name in the text of the review itself. Competing interests and confidentiality policies apply to all reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep manuscripts and correspondence confidential and do not share information about submissions with anyone else unless previously agreed with the editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must not make use of material or take advantage of information obtained through the peer review process. Read the PLOS Confidentiality Policy for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling previously-reviewed manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: If you reviewed the article at another journal, consider the manuscript as a new submission unless instructed otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It may have been revised since last evaluated; PLOS criteria may differ. When you submit your review, inform the editor that you reviewed a previous version at another journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeframe for review completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim to complete your review within 10 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need more time to perform the review, email the journal as soon as possible to request an extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receiving reviewer credit (ORCID)
rubrics_metrics.description: Link your PLOS reviewer account to your ORCID record to have reviewer activity automatically posted to your ORCID profile review activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This confirms you completed a review but will not publish the content of your review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the structured reviewer form
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS Global Public Health uses a structured reviewer form containing two sections: Comments to the author and Comments to the editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In 'Comments to the author' answer questions 1–4 with a drop-down response (e.g., 'Yes','No','I don't know','N/A') and provide details as needed; enter the main text of your peer review in question 5 'Review Comments to the Author'. In 'Comments to the editor' declare competing interests, list collaborators, and optionally indicate whether the submission should be highlighted on the journal webpage.

rubrics_metrics.name: No confidential comments other than competing interests
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS Global Public Health does not allow confidential comments other than the declaration of competing interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have confidential concerns relating to publication or research ethics, contact globalpubhealth@plos.org rather than placing them in the confidential comments field. Reviews must be entered in the submission system; email the journal office if you have trouble accessing the manuscript or entering comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for publication: meet journal policies
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for publication manuscripts must meet PLOS Global Public Health's criteria for publication and comply with editorial and publishing policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This guidance relates especially to articles reporting original research; reviewers should assess compliance with editorial/publishing policies as well as technical quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original research requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The study presents the results of original research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should verify that the manuscript reports original work and is not merely a review or commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: No prior publication of reported results
rubrics_metrics.description: Results reported have not been published elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for duplicate publication, redundant publication, or prior availability of the same results in other outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical standard and sufficient detail in analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiments, statistics, and other analyses are performed to a high technical standard and are described in sufficient detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether statistical methods are appropriate, reported transparently, and described enough to evaluate and reproduce analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusions supported by the data
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclusions are presented in an appropriate fashion and are supported by the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify overinterpretation, unsupported claims, or conclusions not warranted by the results; suggest additional analyses or temper conclusions where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and standard English presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The article is presented in an intelligible fashion and is written in standard English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess organization, clarity of argument, and readability for the intended audience; point out sections needing clearer writing or restructuring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and research integrity compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The research meets all applicable standards for the ethics of experimentation and research integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify appropriate ethical approvals, consent procedures, and adherence to research integrity standards; raise any ethical concerns with the editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to reporting guidelines and data availability standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The article adheres to appropriate reporting guidelines and community standards for data availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check conformity to guidelines such as CONSORT, STROBE, MIAME, QUORUM, and that data availability statements and repository deposition meet community standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing main claims and significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the main claims of the paper and evaluate how significant they are for the discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider novelty, contribution to the field, and whether claims change understanding or practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualization in previous literature and fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the claims properly placed in the context of the previous literature? Have the authors treated the literature fairly?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out important omitted references, misinterpretation of prior work, or biased literature framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and analyses fully support claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Do the data and analyses fully support the claims? If not, what other evidence is required?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify additional analyses, sensitivity checks, or data that would be needed to support the claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol reporting and deviations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a protocol is provided (e.g., for a randomized controlled trial), note any important deviations and whether authors adequately explain them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are encouraged to publish detailed protocols and algorithms as supporting information; indicate when methods warrant such detailed supporting material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods warranting separate protocols/algorithms
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether any particular methods used in the manuscript warrant publication of detailed protocols/algorithms as supporting information online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend uploading protocols or code as supporting materials where appropriate to improve reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential for resubmission / encouragement to revise
rubrics_metrics.description: If the paper is unsuitable for publication in its present form, judge whether the study shows sufficient potential that the authors should be encouraged to resubmit a revised version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete, constructive feedback on what revisions would make the manuscript acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data deposition and identifier reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Are original data deposited in appropriate repositories and are accession/version numbers provided for genes, proteins, mutants, diseases, etc.?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request deposition and accession numbers where missing; point to appropriate repositories if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformity to specific reporting guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the study conform to any relevant guidelines such as CONSORT, MIAME, QUORUM, STROBE, and the Fort Lauderdale agreement?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate missing checklist items or guideline non-compliance and request corrections or clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological detail for reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Are details of the methodology sufficient to allow the experiments to be reproduced?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out missing steps, materials, parameter values, or other information needed to replicate findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of software/code
rubrics_metrics.description: Is any software created by the authors freely available?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request open access to code or indicate acceptable reasons for restricted access; suggest deposition of code in repositories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility to non-specialists
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the manuscript well organized and written clearly enough to be accessible to non-specialists?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend clearer explanations of technical terms, better structure, and lay summaries where appropriate for a broad public health audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct constructive feedback to authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Although confidential comments to the editors are respected, any remarks that might help to strengthen the paper should be directed to the authors themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid placing actionable suggestions only in confidential editor comments; use the 'Comments to the author' section for constructive guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to re-review revised manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are often asked to evaluate revised manuscripts and the authors’ responses to reviewer comments and are encouraged to make themselves available for re-review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate availability for re-review when submitting your initial review, and be prepared to assess authors' responses and revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional language and appropriateness of reviewer comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer comments should be professional; PLOS staff will not change reviewer comments intended for authors except when language is inappropriate for professional communication or contains confidential information or major risk if conveyed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid inappropriate language, unprofessional remarks, or inclusion of confidential materials in the review. If editors have concerns that do not meet edit/remove criteria, they may advise authors they can disregard parts of a reviewer’s comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors' ultimate decision and handling conflicting reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors make the final decision based on reviewers’ comments, the journal's criteria for publication, and their own assessment; conflicting reviews may prompt sharing reviews with other reviewers and requesting additional comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should be aware decisions are not necessarily majority rule; editors may weigh expertise, alignment with policy, or seek further input to resolve conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact points for concerns and help
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have questions or concerns about the manuscript or need assistance submitting the review, contact globalpubhealth@plos.org or use resources like the Peer Review Center and Peer Review Toolbox.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use provided contacts for procedural, ethical, or technical queries rather than placing confidential material in comments.
